title: Interactions in the Environment
seo_title: Grade 8 Natural Sciences: Interactions in the Environment Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 8 Natural Sciences: Interactions and interdependence within the environment
standard_text: Ecosystems have biotic and abiotic factors; organisms are adapted to their environment. Feeding relationships include food chains and webs, and energy flows through trophic levels. Nutrients are recycled; relationships include predation, competition and symbiosis. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 8, Life and Living: Interactions and interdependence within the environment)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): biotic and abiotic factors, adaptation, food webs, energy flow, nutrient cycles and relationships between species. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy flows through an ecosystem; nutrients cycle.
key_sub: About 10% of the energy passes to the next level.
body_html:
How to think about it

An ecosystem has biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living: light, water, temperature, soil) factors. Organisms are adapted to their habitats, for example the gemsbok survives in the Kalahari with little water.

Energy flows from producers to herbivores to carnivores; only about 10% passes to each next trophic level, so there are fewer top predators. Decomposers return nutrients to the soil. Relationships include predation (lion and zebra), competition (for food or space) and symbiosis (oxpeckers and buffalo).

Example

Is temperature a biotic or an abiotic factor?

Is it living?

Answer: abiotic

Example

Why are there fewer lions than zebras?

Energy is lost at each level.

Answer: less energy is available at the top

Common mistakes

  • Thinking energy is recycled like nutrients.
  • Thinking decomposers are not part of food webs.
  • Mixing up biotic and abiotic.
